question: In scikit-learn LogisticRegression, what is the default C and does a smaller C mean stronger or weaker regularization?
answer: The default C in scikit-learn LogisticRegression is 1.0 [S1]. A smaller C means stronger regularization [S1].

citations.text:
3. Regularization Strength in scikit-learn
In scikit-learn LogisticRegression the parameter C is the inverse of the regularization strength: a
smaller C means stronger regularization, and the default is C=1.0. For Ridge regression the
parameter alpha works the opposite way: a larger alpha means stronger shrinkage.
L2 regularization (ridge) shrinks all weights toward zero; L1 regularization (lasso) can set some
weights exactly to zero and therefore performs feature selection.

S9.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S9.text:
1. Reading Learning Curves
A learning curve plots training error and validation error against the training set size. In a high-bias
model both errors are high and they converge close to each other; adding more data barely helps
because the model is too simple. In a high-variance model the training error is low and a large gap
separates it from the validation error; the validation error keeps falling as more data is added, so
collecting more data helps.
When a model is overfitting the first actions to try are a simpler model, stronger regularization,
more training data or early stopping.
